name: Inferact TPU megakernels (agent_space/tpu-megakernels: Qwen3.8-27B + DFlash2, Kimi K3 + DSpark)
scope: Read the decode megakernel code, not only the README: qwen/decode_megakernel.py (single-token transformer_stack, 8-token transformer_stack_block verify kernel, TP prefill/verify references), qwen/load.py (tile schedule, pre-tiled weight layout, padding heuristics), qwen/dflash.py (fused draft kernel, device-side speculation loop), kimi/decode_megakernel.py (93-layer KDA/MLA/MoE stack, VMEM byte pool, cross-layer prefetch, routed-expert stream), kimi/dspark.py (fused draft kernel), pool_alias.py (raw VMEM reinterpret views), collectives32.py (two-level TP32 all-reduce with int16 host packets), plus the companion blog post. Question answered for MegaBake: which parts of the TPU design (one continuous weight stream across op and layer boundaries, compute hidden under that stream, speculative verify that reuses one weight pass for 8 tokens, on-chip buffer aliasing) transfer to a generic SM90 persistent CUDA megakernel, which of them MegaBake already has, and which are only possible because the model runs as one kernel. GPU work was not run; all MegaBake observations are static analysis of src/megabake plus ROADMAP.md, PERFORMANCE_REPORT.md and artifacts/full_model_2026-10-18/*/report.json.

core_ideas.idea: Global cross-op, cross-layer weight bank ring (BANK_COUNT)
core_ideas.how_it_works: All decode weights are enumerated at trace time into one linear tile sequence: per 4-layer block, 3 linear-attention layers (qkvz, outw, gu, dw) then 1 full-attention layer (qwkv, ow, gu, dw), then the LM head. schedule() gives each op a (bk, bn, nk, nb, nt) slot and offsets inside the block. A global index g maps back to (layer, op, tile) arithmetically. VMEM holds BANK_COUNT=12 banks of up to 1024x1280 bf16 (2.5 MB each, ~31 MB total). The prologue starts DMAs for g = 0..11. Every gemv step waits on bank (g % 12), runs the MXU dot, and immediately starts the DMA for g + 12. Because g is global, the refill issued during the last tiles of a GEMV targets the first tiles of the next GEMV, possibly in the next layer or the LM head. The HBM DMA engine therefore always has 12 tiles (~30 MB) in flight, and nothing between GEMVs (norm, conv, delta rule, attention, all-reduce) stalls the weight stream. Weights are stored pre-tiled (tile_matrix) so each bank fill is one contiguous DMA.

core_ideas.idea: Hiding norms, RoPE, attention and gated delta rule under the weight stream
core_ideas.how_it_works: Non-GEMM work runs on the vector/scalar units between gemv calls, while the 12 outstanding bank DMAs keep HBM busy. Each op's small operands are prefetched with their own semaphores at the start of the op and waited only when needed: next-layer norm rows (norm() prefetches li+1 into the same slot), conv state, recurrent state, conv weights, A_log, dt_bias and o-norm before the qkvz GEMV; q/k norm weights before the qwkv GEMV. State writebacks (conv, recurrent) are started asynchronously and waited at the next linear-attention layer. RoPE cos/sin are computed in-kernel once per step from the position. Attention streams 128-key KV tiles double-buffered on a separate DMA queue. The only real stalls are the cross-device all-reduce after outw/ow/dw, which is latency-bound.

core_ideas.idea: Cross-layer prefetch into an aliased VMEM pool (Kimi)
core_ideas.how_it_works: Kimi's projections and expert weights are too large for a uniform bank ring, so Kimi uses a single uint8 VMEM pool sized max(expert pool, attention pool). pool_views() reinterprets byte ranges of the pool as typed tiled memrefs: KDA projections, MLA projections, or 4 expert slots. When the routed-expert stream finishes (the after_experts callback), the next layer's norms, attention projections, KDA aux params and state, MLA norms and router are DMA'd into the freed bytes. This overlaps with the MoE all-reduce and residual work. Layer 0 is peeled out so the loop body contains no conditional that would block the LLO scheduler's overlap.

core_ideas.idea: Raw on-chip buffer aliasing with typed reinterpret views
core_ideas.how_it_works: pool_alias.py monkey-patches Pallas Mosaic lowering (_reshape_memref) so a Reinterpret transform emits tpu.reinterpret_cast with an explicit (8*packing,128) tiled layout. Any byte range of a scratch buffer can then be viewed as any dtype and shape. storage_size() computes the padded tiled footprint. The contract is 'every new view must be overwritten before reading'. Lifetimes are managed by hand: the same bytes hold attention weights, then expert weights, then next-layer attention weights.

core_ideas.idea: Speculative verify reusing one weight pass for 8 tokens (DFlash2 / DSpark)
core_ideas.how_it_works: transformer_stack_block is the decode kernel with B=8 rows (anchor plus 7 drafts) multiplying each streamed weight tile, so the HBM-bound cost is about the same as single-token decode. Attention packs B x GQA-group query rows into one MXU tile and patches the 8 new K/V rows into the streamed cache tile. The gated delta rule runs sequentially over the 8 positions and DMAs a recurrent and conv snapshot per position to HBM (double-buffered snapshot slots), so the host or loop can roll back to the accepted prefix. KV slots past the accepted prefix are overwritten next round. Acceptance is jnp.sum(jnp.cumprod(block[1:] == post[:-1])). make_scan_fn wraps draft kernel, verify kernel, acceptance and state selection in one jax.lax.while_loop on device, so the host does not sync per round. Hidden-state taps from layers (5,19,33,47,61) feed the drafter. Kimi DSpark: the verify kernel at batch 8 is one anchor plus 7 drafts, and the fused draft kernel streams its layer-0 weights behind the fc phase.

core_ideas.idea: In-kernel greedy sampling and embedding gather
core_ideas.how_it_works: The kernel fetches the embedding row for the token (an 8-row aligned DMA plus a select) and computes the LM head through the same bank ring. Each rank takes its argmax, then ranks exchange (max, index) pairs, so the next token id leaves the kernel directly and the host never sees logits on the greedy path.

core_ideas.idea: GQA-group packing into one matrix tile for decode attention
core_ideas.how_it_works: For each KV head, the group's query heads (up to 8) are packed into one 8-row MXU tile. Each K/V tile is loaded once per KV head and shared by all query heads in the group. Online softmax state (m, l, acc) lives in VMEM.

core_ideas.idea: Static, trace-time tile schedule with model-shape-derived tile sizes
core_ideas.how_it_works: tile_hw picks the largest 128-multiple (bk, bn) that divides K/N under env caps QWEN_MAXK/QWEN_MAXN. gu_width and dw_k pad widths when the overhead is at most 6%. The whole schedule is Python constants, and BANK_COUNT is an env var. The README and code contain no autotuner or cost model, so the values were picked by hand for TPU v7 VMEM and these model shapes.

core_ideas.idea: Communication-aware collectives (two-level, quantized) inside the kernel
core_ideas.how_it_works: For TP32, each rank sends its projection partial to its 7 host-local peers, sums them, encodes the host sum as int16 with a shared power-of-two exponent, and exchanges with 3 remote hosts. Slots alternate between reductions, so the next reduction can start while the previous slot's ACKs drain. The Qwen block verify uses a reduce-scatter in f32, rounds once, then all-gathers bf16.

Several overlap decisions are hard-coded by batch size: overlap_kda_state_reads/writes only for batch in (6, 8); persist_kda_state for batch <= 4; attention token scatter only for batch 4 or 8; MoE routed reduce-scatter only for 6 or 8; overlap_latent_gather when selected_expert_count >= 12; block_major only at batch >= 8. Each switch encodes a measured win at one shape.

megabake_status.idea: Global cross-op, cross-layer weight bank ring (BANK_COUNT)
megabake_status.evidence: src/megabake/bodies/gemm.py:700-740 creates a PipelineTmaAsync per GEMM body call. TABLE_GEMM_SHARED_BYTES (gemm.py:1711) fixes 8 stages of 64x64 per CTA. codegen.py:1427-1432 ends each interval with counting_grid_barrier. ROADMAP step 9 (cross-phase L2 weight prefetch) is 'not started'. gemm.py:684-686 prefetches only TMA descriptors.
megabake_status.notes: MegaBake's smem ring is per phase and per CTA. It is filled after the barrier and drained before the next one, so every GEMM phase pays HBM latency plus the fill. PERFORMANCE_REPORT.md:79 calls this out ('every phase pays its pipeline start-up'). The TPU ring never drains. MegaBake already has what a GPU version needs: a static phase table, deterministic CTA rotation (codegen.py:1420 _rotated), and K-major weights where a CTA's 64-row swapAB slab is one contiguous byte range. Each CTA can therefore know its next GEMM tiles statically.

megabake_status.idea: Hiding norms, RoPE, attention and gated delta rule under the weight stream
megabake_status.evidence: ROADMAP.md 5 step 3 note: 1.7B decode spends 0.77 ms outside GEMMs (49 RMSNorms, 24 decode attentions, elementwise). Each runs in its own barrier interval while HBM is idle except for activations. PERFORMANCE_REPORT.md:76: 61 RMSNorm reductions take 0.21 ms on 135M.
megabake_status.notes: Interval folding (step 8) and recompute-by-consumer cut the number of intervals, but no weight bytes move during non-GEMM intervals. Events (step 10) would let independent work overlap, but a norm is a true dependency of the next GEMM's activation operand, not of its weights. Only prefetch can hide the norm under the weight stream.

megabake_status.idea: Cross-layer prefetch into an aliased VMEM pool (Kimi)
megabake_status.evidence: No data prefetch in src/megabake (grep for prefetch finds only gemm.py:684-686 descriptor prefetch).
megabake_status.notes: On GPU the analog is L2 prefetch (cp.async.bulk.prefetch.L2 / cp.async.bulk.prefetch.tensor.L2) issued by idle CTAs or a dedicated warp, because per-SM smem (228 KB) is far smaller than a layer's weights. The VMEM pool is 64 MiB, while the L2 share of the MIG 3g slice is roughly 20-25 MB [uncertain].

megabake_status.idea: Raw on-chip buffer aliasing with typed reinterpret views
megabake_status.evidence: codegen.py:1916-1933 sizes generic-body smem as the max over phases (union). memory.py does lifetime-based best-fit reuse of global workspace. But codegen.py:591-592 and 1226-1230 add GEMM stage bytes to the generic union instead of overlaying them. PERFORMANCE_REPORT.md:278 records that sequential GEMM variants sum their scratch, and codegen.py:1222 requires every table GEMM to share one tile and smem layout.
megabake_status.notes: Overlaying GEMM stages with generic scratch is safe, because a CTA runs one body at a time (codegen.py:1449 sync_threads before reuse). It would free ~10-40 KB for more stages or a cross-phase weight prefetch buffer. It would also allow per-GEMM tile variants with max() sizing, the same way Kimi sizes its pool.

megabake_status.idea: Speculative verify reusing one weight pass for 8 tokens (DFlash2 / DSpark)
megabake_status.evidence: No speculation, draft or verify code in src/megabake. ARCHITECTURE.md:295 mentions draft count only as a workload fact. megabake::kv_attention is one-token decode (fx_handler/hf_attention.py:12,120). swapAB tiles of 16/32/64 rows (gemm.py:1888-1896) already make an 8-row GEMM cost about the same as 1 row.
megabake_status.notes: The GEMM side is ready: an 8-row verify step should cost about the same as a 1-row decode step, because GEMMs are weight-bound and swapAB pads to a 16-row tile anyway. Missing pieces: multi-query kv_attention with causal masking inside the draft block and KV write of B rows, acceptance and rollback, a device-side loop (CUDA graph conditional while node or in-kernel), and, for GDN models, per-position recurrent-state snapshots.

megabake_status.idea: In-kernel greedy sampling and embedding gather
megabake_status.evidence: Embedding is part of the captured graph and runs in-kernel. main.py:204 does argmax on the host side for checking only. No sampling op is lowered.
megabake_status.notes: An argmax/top-k reduction body at the end of the kernel is generic (reduction family). It removes a launch and makes a device-side multi-step loop possible.

megabake_status.idea: GQA-group packing into one matrix tile for decode attention
megabake_status.evidence: bodies/attention.py:258-290: 'one query row per warp', and the head_grouping fact is used for indexing. Split-context chunks (attention.py:420-423).
megabake_status.notes: Whether warps in a GQA group share K/V tiles through smem or each re-read from L2 was not determined [uncertain]. The TPU kernel loads each K/V tile once per KV head and uses a matrix unit for QK^T and PV. On SM90 the equivalent is an mma over the group's query rows (FlashDecoding/FlashInfer style).

megabake_status.idea: Static, trace-time tile schedule with model-shape-derived tile sizes
megabake_status.evidence: plan.py/planner.py plan search, phase table, size buckets (buckets.py). Table GEMM tile is fixed at (token_tile, 64) with 8 stages (gemm.py:1853-1876).
megabake_status.notes: MegaBake is more generic than the TPU code, which hand-picks tiles per model, but the table GEMM has only one candidate. See generality_and_overfitting_risk.

megabake_status.idea: Communication-aware collectives (two-level, quantized) inside the kernel
megabake_status.evidence: MegaBake targets a single GPU (H200 MIG slice); no TP.
megabake_status.notes: Relevant only if multi-GPU TP is added later. Then NVSHMEM/NVLink put-based all-reduce inside the kernel follows the same pattern.

megabake_status.evidence: MegaBake has similar shape gates: SWAP_AB_MAX_ROWS=64, SWAP_AB_ROW_TILES=(16,32,64) (gemm.py:1888-1896), split-K off by default after 'no gain on the 60-SM slice' (ROADMAP 6), DECODE_MAX_CHUNKS=16 and DECODE_MIN_CHUNK_KEYS=64 (attention.py:421-422).
megabake_status.notes: This is the same risk the TPU code takes on deliberately. MegaBake should not copy it.

megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.opportunity: Unbounded-lookahead weight stream across op and layer boundaries (bank ring through barriers)
megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.why_multi_kernel_cannot: In a kernel graph, kernel N+1's producer warps cannot start until kernel N's CTAs retire, or, with PDL, until N calls the launch trigger and SM resources free up. A decode GEMM that fills all SMs (persistent, one CTA per SM by smem) leaves no room for N+1's CTAs to be co-resident, and the smem ring of N cannot be handed to N+1. Lookahead is therefore at most one kernel and opportunistic: the CUDA guide says PDL overlap 'is not guaranteed'. In a persistent megakernel, the same CTA, with smem and mbarriers alive, can issue weight TMA loads for phase p+1, p+2, ... before it reaches the grid barrier of phase p. Weights have no data dependency on activations, and the static phase table tells each CTA exactly which tiles it will own next.
megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.nearest_multi_kernel_substitute: PDL with a pre-cudaGridDependencySynchronize prologue that prefetches the kernel's own first weight tiles to smem or L2. This saves part of one fill per kernel when there is room for co-residency, and nothing across norm/attention kernels that sit between GEMMs.

megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.opportunity: Keeping HBM busy during non-GEMM phases (norm, RoPE, attention, GDN, barriers)
megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.why_multi_kernel_cannot: Between kernels, no one owns the DMA engines. A norm kernel issues only its own activation loads, and the next GEMM's weight stream cannot start until the norm finishes (or the PDL trigger). In MegaBake, any CTA idle or waiting in a barrier can issue cp.async.bulk.prefetch.L2 for the next GEMM's weight slabs during the norm and attention intervals. With events (step 10), a dedicated subset of CTAs could run the next GEMM's weight-only producer while others compute the norm.
megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.nearest_multi_kernel_substitute: A side stream running an L2-prefetch kernel concurrently with norm and attention kernels. This works in principle but is brittle: it needs free SMs, it contends with the main kernel for scheduling, and it cannot be ordered tightly with CUDA Graph capture.

megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.opportunity: One on-chip buffer pool with phase-dependent typed views (GEMM stages and generic scratch overlaid)
megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.why_multi_kernel_cannot: Every kernel gets its own smem allocation, so nothing persists across kernels and there is nothing to alias. In a megakernel, smem allocated once can serve as GEMM stages in one phase, norm scratch in the next, and a prefetch staging buffer that survives from a non-GEMM phase into the GEMM that consumes it. This is what makes 'prefetch into smem across a barrier' possible at all.
megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.nearest_multi_kernel_substitute: None. Distributed shared memory and L2 persistence (cudaAccessPolicyWindow) are the closest, and L2 persistence is coarse and global.

megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.opportunity: Device-resident speculative loop with in-kernel acceptance and state rollback
megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.why_multi_kernel_cannot: Partially replicable: CUDA 12.4+ graph conditional (while) nodes or a JAX-style while_loop can loop draft, verify and accept on device. A megakernel can also fuse the draft model and the verify into one launch, pipelining the draft's weight stream behind the verify's tail (as dspark.py streams layer-0 weights behind fc), and keep acceptance and state selection in-kernel without separate kernels for snapshot selection.
megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.nearest_multi_kernel_substitute: CUDA graph with conditional while node plus separate draft, verify, accept and select kernels. This gets most of the host-sync savings but not the cross-model weight-stream overlap.

megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.opportunity: Zero-cost small-operand prefetch (norm weights, biases, conv/recurrent state) one layer ahead
megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.why_multi_kernel_cannot: A multi-kernel graph can only load these at the start of each kernel, where the load is on the critical path. In a persistent kernel, the CTA that will run layer l+1's norm can load gamma during layer l. This is small (a few KB) but removes a dependent HBM round trip (~1 us) per norm phase.
megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.nearest_multi_kernel_substitute: Fusing the norm into the GEMM prologue (Mirage rmsnorm_linear). This removes the separate phase but still loads gamma on the critical path.

measured_or_reported_gains: Reported by Inferact (README, blog, Sept 2026): Kimi K3 + DSpark at acceptance length 6 reaches 709 accepted tok/s on 16x TPU v7 vs 452 on 16x GB200 (1.57x). Qwen3.8-27B + DFlash2 reaches 1,515 vs 695 tok/s on 4x TPU v7 vs 4x GB200 (2.18x). Without speculation, decode is about 1.4-2x the GB200 baseline at batch 1-8, with the largest lead at batch 1. A Kimi verify step (batch 8 = 1 anchor + 7 drafts) takes about 8.5 ms. The full megakernel compiles in under 90 s, versus 30+ minutes for comparable XLA. The blog gives no HBM-utilization percentage and no per-mechanism ablation numbers; the qwen kernel exposes ablation switches (noexchange, nodelta, noattn, noaux, nocompute) but no published results [uncertain]. The GB200 baseline software stack is not specified in the code [uncertain]. TPU v7 HBM is 7.38 TB/s vs 8 TB/s for GB200, so a TPU win at batch 1 implies the TPU kernel sustains a much higher fraction of peak HBM bandwidth than the GPU baseline. That inference is ours, not measured [uncertain].
expected_impact_on_megabake: Baseline, SmolLM-1.7B decode (artifacts/full_model_2026-10-18): MegaBake kernel 2.974 ms vs Inductor kernels 2.425 ms. Weight floor ~1.55 ms (3.4 GB at 2.2 TB/s). GEMMs ~1.92 ms at ~1.8 TB/s over 169 GEMM phases. ~0.77-1.0 ms is non-GEMM plus barrier time: 49 RMSNorm at ~2.8 us = 0.14 ms, 24 decode attentions at ~10 us = 0.24 ms, ~6 barrier intervals per layer at 0.7 us = ~0.1 ms, and elementwise. Ranked estimates: (1) Cross-phase smem weight prefetch: the producer warp issues TMA for the first S stages of the CTA's next-GEMM weight slab before entering the grid barrier, and only the activation operand waits. Removing a ~1-2 us fill/latency bubble from each of 169 GEMM phases saves ~0.17-0.34 ms (6-11%) [uncertain]. Generic, no model knowledge. (2) L2 weight prefetch during non-GEMM intervals (ROADMAP step 9): HBM is nearly idle for ~0.5-0.8 ms per step. With a ~20-25 MB L2 share [uncertain], each 3 us norm interval can prefetch ~6.6 MB (the first ~25-50% of the following QKV or gate/up projection). A 10 us attention interval could prefetch 22 MB but would hit the L2 capacity limit. Expect 0.15-0.35 ms saved (5-12%), bringing the 1.7B kernel to about 2.3-2.6 ms, near Inductor's 2.42 ms of kernels. The step-9 exit criterion (GEMMs >= 1.9 TB/s effective) is consistent with this. 135M decode (1.50 ms vs 1.38 ms) is dominated by latency rather than weight bytes (~0.27 GB, floor ~0.12 ms), so prefetch helps less (~0.05-0.1 ms). Barrier and fill elimination via events matter more there. (3) Speculative verify at 8 rows: per-step kernel time would stay roughly 3.0 ms on 1.7B, because swapAB already pads to a 16-row tile. Throughput would scale with acceptance length: 2-4x tokens/s at acceptance 3-4, the largest effect on decode tokens/s. It needs multi-query kv_attention, rollback, and a draft source (a generic n-gram or prompt-lookup draft avoids a model-specific drafter) [uncertain on acceptance rates]. (4) Overlaying GEMM stages with generic smem: no direct speedup, but it frees room for the prefetch staging in (1) and for per-GEMM tile variants. (5) GQA-group-shared KV tiles in decode attention: up to group-size (3x for 1.7B with 32/... heads [uncertain]) less KV traffic. Matters at long context: at 2,000 cached tokens the 1.7B decode is 5.5 ms vs 2.66 ms at 16 tokens, so up to ~1-2 ms there [uncertain]. (6) In-kernel argmax: ~10-30 us of host/launch per token, and a prerequisite for device-side multi-token loops. Prefill (>64 tokens) is compute- and attention-bound, not weight-stream-bound, so ideas 1-2 give little there. Its gaps are the prefill attention body and the >64-row GEMM path.
generality_and_overfitting_risk: The reference itself is explicitly per-model and per-hardware. BANK_COUNT=12 and the tile caps 1024x1280 come from env vars tuned for 64 MiB VMEM (qwen/decode_megakernel.py:27-29; qwen/load.py:270-278). The 4-layer block structure (layers%4, head_dim=256, GQA group <= 8) is hard-coded (qwen/decode_megakernel.py:347-350, 383). The gu_width padding uses magic 1280/512/6% (load.py:291-306). Kimi's batch-size switches (kimi/decode_megakernel.py:3700-3720, 1514) and layer index 92 checks (3936, 3942) are also hard-coded. Take the mechanism (static global tile order plus lookahead ring), not the constants. A generic version derives lookahead depth from Little's law (bytes in flight = bandwidth x latency, both measurable or queryable per device) and smem/L2 capacity, not from a model. MegaBake items that look tuned to the tested models or the 60-SM slice: (a) TABLE_GEMM_SHARED_BYTES with exactly 8 stages of 64x64x64 and 4 epilogue stages (src/megabake/bodies/gemm.py:1708-1711). It is the only table-GEMM candidate (gemm.py:1853-1876), and the stage count is not derived from target smem or the prefetch need. (b) SWAP_AB_MAX_ROWS=64 and SWAP_AB_ROW_TILES=(16,32,64) (gemm.py:1888-1896); the 'doubles decode GEMM bandwidth on 60 SMs' justification is measured on the slice only. (c) Split-K is off by default because it showed 'no gain on the 60-SM slice' (ROADMAP 6; compiler.py:422 MEGABAKE_SPLIT_K env). On a full 132-SM H200 or on B200, small-N projections leave many more SMs idle, so this decision may flip. (d) SPLIT_K_MAX=16 and SPLIT_K_MIN_K_TILES=2 (gemm.py:1907-1909). (e) DECODE_MAX_CHUNKS=16 and DECODE_MIN_CHUNK_KEYS=64 (bodies/attention.py:421-422). (f) Fixed (64,64)/13 stages and (64,128)/8 stages for non-table launches (gemm.py:1879-1883). (g) Interval folding and recompute thresholds were tuned on SmolLM-135M (ROADMAP step 8 exit criterion is a 135M number). In split_k_count and the schedule, target.multiprocessor_count is queried from the device (compiler.py:1512; runtime.py:265 checks it), which is good. How references avoid overfitting: Mirage MPK splits linears into worker-count-dependent task counts. CUTLASS derives stage counts from smem capacity (_compute_stages here at gemm.py:1245-1291, bypassed by the fixed table budget). Inductor autotunes GEMM templates. For a GPU bank ring, MegaBake should compute prefetch depth per phase as min(L2 share or smem budget, bandwidth x (non-GEMM interval estimate + HBM latency)). Bandwidth and L2 size come from a startup microbenchmark or cudaDeviceProp (l2CacheSize, persistingL2CacheMaxSize). Keep the sizing in a cost model or measured autotune, not in constants.
hardware_portability: Bank-ring and lookahead concept: hardware-generic. On TPU it is explicit DMA into VMEM. On GPU it maps to (1) cp.async.bulk.tensor (TMA) into a persistent smem ring that the producer warp advances across phases (SM90+), (2) cp.async.bulk.prefetch.L2 / prefetch.tensor.L2 for deeper lookahead (SM90+), and (3) on SM80, cp.async 16-byte copies plus prefetch.global.L2 PTX instructions (no TMA, so a full warp issues the copies). On SM100 (B200/GB200): TMA and L2 prefetch carry over unchanged. WGMMA is replaced by tcgen05.mma with accumulators in TMEM. The 2-SM CTA pair (cta_group::2) shares B operand loads. CLC (cluster launch control) offers dynamic persistent scheduling, but a static phase table still decides prefetch targets. The bigger SM100 smem/TMEM budget and 8 TB/s HBM make the ring deeper (Little's law), so depth must not be a constant. TMA multicast across a cluster helps prefill and batched GEMMs, where several CTAs share one weight tile across M-tiles. In swapAB decode each CTA owns distinct weight rows, so multicast only saves activation-operand traffic, which is tiny. It is not a decode win. setmaxnreg (SM90) matters only for producer/consumer warp specialization of the cross-phase producer. Note PERFORMANCE_REPORT.md:287: warps that executed setmaxregister_decrease(40) later run generic bodies, so a persistent producer warp across phases must keep its register budget consistent. VMEM pool aliasing maps to smem union; it is generic and simpler on GPU (raw byte offsets). Collectives: NVLink/NVSHMEM on multi-GPU; not applicable now. To stay target-generic: put 'weight-tile stream order' and 'prefetch depth' into the plan as target-independent IR (per CTA: list of future (address, bytes) slabs). Let body providers per target (SM90 TMA, SM100 TMA+tcgen05, SM80 cp.async) implement 'issue prefetch' and 'consume stage', with depth from target properties.

recommended_actions.action: Cross-phase weight-only smem prefetch: split the table GEMM mainloop pipeline so weight stages (A in swapAB) and activation stages (B) have separate full barriers. Before each grid barrier, the producer warp of each CTA issues TMA for the first S weight stages of the GEMM tile that CTA will own in the next GEMM phase (known statically from phase_table plus rotation). The consumer waits on the barrier only for activations. Keep pipeline mbarriers and phase bits alive across phases instead of recreating PipelineTmaAsync per call.

recommended_actions.prerequisite: Static per-CTA tile assignment for GEMM phases (exists via rotation); GEMM must not reuse weight-stage smem with generic scratch while a prefetch is in flight.

recommended_actions.action: ROADMAP step 9, L2 weight prefetch during non-GEMM intervals: in every interval whose phases are not GEMMs (norm, RoPE, attention, elementwise), have each CTA issue cp.async.bulk.prefetch.L2 for its contiguous 64-row x K weight slab of the next one or two GEMM phases, capped by a per-target L2 budget from cudaDeviceProp.l2CacheSize and the MIG slice share. Emit the prefetch list as a plan-level per-phase annotation, so later events and SM100 backends reuse it.
